chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd said to him: “I have daughters.”

He said: “Perhaps you wish for their death. Indeed, if you were to wish for their death and they died, you would not be rewarded on the Day of Resurrection, and you would meet your Lord, when you meet Him, while you are disobedient.”

key_terms.بَنَاتٍ: daughters; female children who are the subject of the statement
key_terms.تَتَمَنَّى: you wish; to desire or hope for something to occur
key_terms.تُؤْجَرْ: you will be rewarded; to receive divine reward
key_terms.رَبَّكَ: your Lord; Allah, whom the servant will meet
key_terms.عَاصٍ: disobedient; one in a state of sin or defiance
key_terms.مَوْتَهُنَّ: their death; the death of the daughters being wished for
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection; the final day of reckoning

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about wishing for the death of one’s daughters?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns wishing for the death of one’s daughters and treats such a wish as an act of disobedience to Allah. It teaches that children are a means of reward, and that resenting their existence deprives a person of spiritual merit and affects their standing in the Hereafter.
